question: In the synthetic 4,000-person extract supplied with the task, what is the average effect on the treated (ATT) of enrolling in the voluntary 1976-77 job-training program (the enrolment indicator in the file) on participants' 1978 earnings (re78), under the assumption that enrolment is independent of potential outcomes given eleven pre-program covariates (age, educ, married, urban, region, children, health_limit, re74, re75, unemp74, unemp75), and is that effect smaller in magnitude than $1,000?
hypotheses: H1 (primary): the ATT on re78 is zero; two-sided test at 5%. The paper reports the point estimate and 95% confidence interval and never states 'no effect' on the basis of a non-rejection alone.

H1b (equivalence, primary): the ATT on re78 lies within (-$1,000, +$1,000); two one-sided tests at 5% (equivalently, the 90% CI inside the margin). The margin is fixed now, before any outcome is examined, from context: the experimental benchmark for a comparable program is $1,794 in 1982 dollars (Dehejia & Wahba) and short-run effects across many evaluations average close to zero (Card, Kluve & Weber 2018). Only if H1b is supported may the paper say the effect is smaller than $1,000.

H2 (secondary family): the ATTs on re79, employed78, hours78, benefits78 and wellbeing78. Each is reported with its estimate, a Romano-Wolf familywise-adjusted p-value over these five outcomes, and simultaneous (max-t) 95% confidence intervals; uncorrected p-values are shown next to adjusted ones.
contribution: A pre-specified observational evaluation in which the estimand, the conditioning set, the closed list of outcomes and their multiple-testing corrections, and an equivalence margin are all fixed while every outcome is still unexamined, with every analysed outcome reported. The data are synthetic; no claim is made about any real program.

tasks.title: Prior work on evaluating job-training programs with observational data; methods for selection on observables

outcomes.not_analysed: survey_q01-survey_q20: their timing relative to the program is not documented, so they can be neither confounders nor outcomes with confidence. They are not used as covariates and not analysed as outcomes; this is stated as a limitation.
outcomes.relative_effect_denominator: The ATT as a percentage of participants' estimated counterfactual mean re78 (mean re78 of participants minus the ATT), not the non-participant mean.
